newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia stocks mixed on record-high Bogota volume.
newsitem.headline: Colombia stocks mixed on record-high Bogota volume.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed Monday as volume in Bogota climbed to an all-time high with the sale of 48.7 million shares of Banco Santander Colombia, formerly known as Bancoquia.

Bogota's IBB index ended up a wafer-thin 0.14 percent at 1,198.74 on trading of 159 billion pesos, while Medellin's IBOMED index dipped 0.18 percent. Volumes in Medellin were unavailable because of technical problems.
Santander Investment, a unit of Spain's Banco Santander SAN.MC, paid 155 billion pesos to Bavaria SA for a 55 percent stake in Banco Santander Colombia.
Colombia's eighth-largest bank had changed its name at the beginning of the month in preparation for the takeover, which was agreed in principle in May. Bavaria retains a 26 percent stake.
Shares of Banco Santander Colombia climbed 0.47 percent to 3,200 pesos on the deal.
One Bogota dealer said he thought the stock price would drop back in the coming days given that the price paid by Santander Investment was seen as the current ceiling.
Bavaria, Colombia's leading brewer, gained 0.38 percent in Bogota to close at 8,131 and closed up 1.23 percent in Medellin at 8,100.
One of the day's biggest decliners was Cemento Argos, down 1.1 percent to 8,750 in Bogota and down 1.58 percent to 8,710 in Medellin.
